chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who wishes to recite the Tashahhud, the supplications in bowing (Ruku'), prostration (Sujood), and Qunut aloud. He said: 'If he wishes, he may do so; and if he wishes, he may not.'

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: Tashahhud (testimony of faith recited in prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite the prayer supplications aloud or silently?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the flexibility (ikhtiyar) in the manner of recitation for specific supplications and remembrances within the prayer, distinguishing them from obligatory recitations like Surah Al-Fatiha. It reflects the Shia juristic view that while the core pillars must be performed with precision, the recitation of Tashahhud, Ruku', and Sujood dhikr allows for both audible (jahr) and silent (ikhfa) modes based on personal preference or context. This ruling underscores the practical ease (taysir) granted to the worshipper in the non-obligatory components of the ritual prayer.
